title: AI agents are coming to Rivian’s cars
key_facts: RJ Scaringe, founder and chief executive of Rivian, spoke at TechCrunch Disrupt this week.
Rivian recently launched an AI assistant for voice control of its electric vehicles.
In future cars will run agents from other companies, such as Anthropic.
No timing; Rivian points to its AI & Autonomy Day in December.
Rivian built an in-house agentic framework that routes requests to local or cloud models.
Since May the agent could access external apps like Google Calendar.
Vehicle-level controls such as braking and steering are not handed to an agent.
quote_evidence: But the carmaker's founder and CEO, RJ Scaringe, said at TechCrunch Disrupt this week that, in the future, Rivian's cars will be able to run AI agents made by other companies like Anthropic.
"You wouldn't want an agent to determine, 'hey, it's time to apply the brakes, or time to steer the vehicle.'"
why_it_matters_hint: In-car assistants are heading toward third-party AI agents, with safety limits.
